name: Password Sign-In Requires Passkey
summary: The user submits valid password credentials for an identity that requires passkey proof; the server returns the generic MFA-required outcome with provider=passkey and the client routes to the canonical passkey continuation surface.

preconditions.expression: session-capability == anonymous and an active, fully configured password-enabled durable identity with a registered passkey is ready for sign-in

inputs.name: Email
inputs.description: Prepared test-user email resolved by the server before the runner plan is returned.

inputs.name: Password
inputs.description: Valid password generated by the test setup manager and resolved by the server before the runner plan is returned.

serverInteraction.intent: Submit the password through the normal password-sign-in flow and receive the generic MFA-required server outcome; provider=passkey selects the client destination.

postconditions.expression: the password proof has succeeded, no authenticated application session is active, and the client has routed the provider=passkey result to auth.continue.passkey

sourceReferences.note: Expected client destination is the existing canonical Passkey Sign In continuation view.
Once the handoff reaches auth.continue.passkey, the existing Passkey Sign In behavior owns the passkey ceremony and authenticated-session completion.
The server transition is generic MFA Required and does not own the passkey destination.
Response-directed routing is a client presentation obligation; provider-specific routing does not require a distinct C# flow proof.
